chose: A bite taken on an offer of the snap to come is matched to that snap: the first play from scrimmage or kickoff home had not seen when the offer was on its screen, skipping plays a flag wiped out, and only if the scenario's rule accepts it (a play call on 1st and 10 stays unmatched rather than taking the next short-yardage call). An offer of a first possession or a red-zone trip takes the first accepted play of that possession from the snap on. The offer was on home's screen at the bite's start, or reconcile::LAG (5 s) before it when home no longer offered the scenario at the start but did then (the phone had not yet heard). Stored as method `next` with a signed gap. Whether an offer was of the snap to come is decided per moment by the engine replayed at that time (rules::offered_said, one arm per Moment): kick is the snap to come on 4th down but the touchdown's own play while a try is pending, and the try (two-point) looks back to its touchdown, because ESPN writes the try into the touchdown's play. Every bite not taken on an offer still looks back.
options: Anchor on the snap home had not yet seen when the offer was on its screen (chosen): no broadcast-delay constant, and the snap the offer named is by construction not yet in home's log.
Look ahead by a lead-time constant from the bite's start: needs a guessed broadcast delay, and a delayed broadcast puts the snap's wallclock before the bite.
Keep the offer's snap with the bite at recording time (a phone and wire change): exact, but needs some-ui and leaves every bite already kept unfixed.
Direction by scenario alone, as #3040 suggested: wrong for the kick while a try is pending, and for the try itself.
gray: The issue's suggested fix named the try as a pre-snap scenario; the recorded game shows the try is part of its touchdown's play, so the call departs from the suggestion. LAG's 5 s is a judgement of the socket's push plus GW5's 2 s clock error, applied only when home had already stopped offering the scenario at the bite's start, so a quick tap on a new offer never takes the play before it.
undo: Make rules::offered_said return Said::After for every moment (every bite looks back again); rows already stored as `next` stay, and the down migration refuses while any is held.
